sections.title: Spirometry basics
notes: Full breath in, blow out as hard as possible for at least 6 seconds, repeat 3 times, take the best.
**FVC** normal or slightly low in asthma, **low in restrictive disease**. **FEV1** low in both.
**FEV1/FVC ratio separates them**: low in asthma (obstruction), normal or high in restrictive disease.
**FEF 25-75** is the most sensitive marker of obstruction, may be the only abnormal value in mild asthma.

sections.title: Volume-time curve and flow-volume loop
notes: Normal: 75% of FVC out in the first second. Asthma: slower, FVC usually normal.
Flow-volume loop: **scooped (concave) expiratory limb in asthma**, deeper scoop means more severe.
**Flattened inspiratory limb: variable extrathoracic obstruction** (vocal cord paralysis or dysfunction).
Restrictive: **normal shape but small loop**.

sections.title: Reading a spirometry report
notes: Start with **FEV1/FVC**. Low: obstruction. Normal or high: check FVC (normal = normal lung, low = restrictive).
Asthma: low ratio, normal FVC, low FEF 25-75. **Reversibility: 12% or more rise in FEV1** after bronchodilator.

sections.title: Pulse oximetry and blood gases
notes: False readings: nail polish, dyes, bright light, **poor perfusion** (shock, hypothermia).
**Methemoglobinemia and carbon monoxide** give falsely normal sats: use an **arterial blood gas** (co-oximetry).
A warm sample left sitting gives false acidosis (WBCs use oxygen).

sections.title: Stridor by level
notes: Above the glottis: **inspiratory** (epiglottitis). At or below the glottis: **biphasic** (croup, bacterial tracheitis). Intrathoracic: **expiratory** (wheeze, asthma).

sections.title: Epiglottitis vs croup vs bacterial tracheitis
notes: **Epiglottitis**: supraglottic, 2 to 6 years, rapid onset, **toxic, drooling, tripod**, anxious, hoarseness rare. H influenzae (less with vaccine).
**Croup**: subglottic, **6 to 36 months**, URI first, **barking cough**, hoarse, not toxic, often sudden at night. **Parainfluenza**.
**Bacterial tracheitis**: 3 months to 6 years, rapid, **high fever, toxic**, no drooling. **S aureus**.

sections.title: Retropharyngeal abscess
notes: Under 6 years: high fever, **dysphagia, drooling, neck stiffness or hyperextension**, stridor, posterior pharyngeal bulge.
Lateral neck x-ray: **prevertebral soft tissue wider than the vertebral body**. CT: hypodense collection with rim enhancement.
Spreads to the mediastinum or epidural space. Rash with it: think Kawasaki or scarlet fever.
Secure the airway, cultures, **ampicillin-sulbactam or clindamycin**, ENT to drain.

sections.title: Peritonsillar abscess
notes: **Adolescents**: severe sore throat, **trismus**, **hot potato voice**, **uvula deviated away**.
Clinical diagnosis, no imaging needed. **Incision and drainage** gives fast relief.

sections.title: Spasmodic croup
notes: 1 to 3 years, recurrent sudden **night-time** croup that resolves quickly. Linked to **reflux**, allergy, psychological factors.

sections.title: Laryngomalacia
notes: **Most common cause of inspiratory stridor in infants** (75% of chronic stridor).
**Worse supine, crying or feeding, better prone**. Normal cry, normal growth: clinical diagnosis.
Scope if severe, feeding trouble, poor growth. **Gets worse before better**, gone by 1 to 2 years. Surgery only if severe.

sections.title: Vascular ring
notes: Case: 2-week-old, **biphasic stridor that doesn't change with position or bronchodilator**, **right-sided aortic arch** on x-ray: vascular ring.
Most common: **right aortic arch and double aortic arch** encircling trachea and esophagus. Screen for **22q11 deletion**.
**Barium swallow** shows esophageal indentation. **CT or MRI** for anatomy. Treatment is surgery.

sections.title: Vocal cord paralysis
notes: **Second most common cause of infant stridor**. Unilateral: birth or **cardiac surgery** trauma, **weak cry**, better lying on the paralyzed side.
Bilateral: high-pitched biphasic stridor, severe distress. Look for **Arnold-Chiari** or raised intracranial pressure: **head MRI**.
Diagnosis: flexible laryngoscopy. Traumatic often recovers by 6 months. Bilateral may need tracheostomy.

sections.title: Webs, hemangioma, papilloma, nodules
notes: **Laryngeal web**: weak cry and biphasic stridor, surgery if significant.
**Subglottic hemangioma**: half have **skin hemangiomas of the head and neck** (beard area). Stridor grows with the hemangioma. Treat with **propranolol**.
**Laryngeal papillomas**: HPV 6 and 11 from the birth canal, **hoarseness**. Surgical removal.
**Vocal nodules**: most common cause of chronic hoarseness (voice overuse, reflux). Voice rest.

sections.title: Subglottic stenosis and tracheomalacia
notes: Subglottic stenosis: mostly **acquired from prolonged intubation**. Biphasic stridor.
**Tracheomalacia**: expiratory wheeze, **honking cough**, worse supine. Associated with **TE fistula and esophageal atresia**.

sections.title: Cough: clues
notes: Cough receptors from nose to lung (rhinitis, pharyngitis, sinusitis, even the ear canal).
Staccato: **chlamydia** in infants. Whoop: pertussis. **Stops during sleep: habit or psychogenic cough**. Barking: croup, tracheomalacia.
With eating: aspiration, reflux, **H-type TE fistula**. Throat clearing: postnasal drip. Night cough: sinusitis, asthma. Immunocompromised: PJP, TB, CMV.

sections.title: Exposures and regional infections
notes: Birds: psittacosis. Rodents: plague, **hantavirus**. Rabbits: tularemia. Sheep and cattle: **Q fever**.
**Histoplasmosis**: Ohio and Mississippi valleys (bird and bat droppings). **Coccidioidomycosis**: US southwest. Blastomycosis: north and midwest.

sections.title: Chronic cough workup
notes: Purulent chronic sputum: bronchiectasis. Cough with anemia: **pulmonary hemosiderosis**. Nasal polyps, rectal prolapse, failure to thrive: **cystic fibrosis**.
**Cough over 6 weeks without an explanation: sweat chloride test**. Over 3 weeks: chest x-ray, spirometry, CBC, urinalysis.

sections.title: Clubbing and hemoptysis
notes: Clubbing (hypertrophic pulmonary osteoarthropathy): **cyanotic heart disease** most common, **cystic fibrosis** most common lung cause, biliary cirrhosis, endocarditis, familial.
Lost nail angle (Schamroth diamond gone).
Coughed blood is bright red. **Check the nose first**.

sections.title: Hemoptysis causes and workup
notes: Foreign body, abscess, pneumonia, TB, CF, **idiopathic pulmonary hemosiderosis**, AVM, PE, pulmonary endometriosis (cyclic in girls).
Vasculitis: lupus, **Goodpasture**, granulomatosis with polyangiitis (check urine and kidneys). Churg-Strauss: asthma, eosinophilia, nasal polyps.
Check nose and throat first. **Acidic dark blood: stomach. Alkaline bright red: lung**.

sections.title: Croup: presentation and severity
notes: Laryngotracheobronchitis, **parainfluenza** most common. Subglottic narrowing, 3 months to 3 years.
URI then **barking cough**, inspiratory or biphasic stridor, hoarse voice.
**Clinical diagnosis**. Steeple sign may or may not be seen.
Mild: occasional bark, no stridor at rest. Moderate: **stridor at rest**. Severe: persistent stridor, marked retractions, agitation.

sections.title: Croup: management
notes: **Dexamethasone 0.6 mg/kg** (oral, IM or IV, long half-life) for all severities, even mild.
Moderate to severe: **nebulized epinephrine** (no rebound) plus oxygen. Heliox for severe.
Discharge after epinephrine if no stridor at rest, good air entry, normal colour and alertness, dexamethasone given.
Admit: persistent distress, hypoxia, can't drink, **2 or more epinephrine nebs**. Intubate early with a tube 0.5 to 1 mm smaller.

sections.title: Bacterial tracheitis
notes: **S aureus** (also Moraxella, strep), about 4 years. Looks like croup but **toxic, high fever, no response to epinephrine or steroids**.
Can lie flat, no drooling (epiglottitis: sits forward, tripod, drools).
Purulent secretions obstruct: **about 50% need intubation**. Antistaphylococcal antibiotics (nafcillin or vancomycin). Complications: toxic shock, ARDS.

sections.title: Common cold and its mimics
notes: **Green or thick discharge doesn't mean bacterial infection or sinusitis**. Cough medicines don't help young children.
First-generation antihistamines reduce rhinorrhea, second-generation don't.
Allergic rhinitis: itching, sneezing, nasal eosinophils. **Unilateral foul or bloody discharge: nasal foreign body**.
Sinusitis: discharge **over 10 to 14 days**, or high fever with headache and facial pain. Strep nasal infection: crusting around the nostrils.

sections.title: Bronchiolitis
notes: Most common lower respiratory infection **under 2 years**. **RSV over 50%**. RSV-negative: **human metapneumovirus**, parainfluenza, adenovirus, rhinovirus.
Risk for later asthma: maternal asthma or smoking, eczema under 1 year.
URI, then **tachypnea (earliest, most sensitive sign)**, retractions, crackles and wheeze. **Apnea may be the only sign under 2 months or in ex-preemies**.
**Worst on days 3 to 4**.

sections.title: Bronchiolitis: diagnosis and management
notes: **Clinical diagnosis**, no x-ray or blood work. X-ray if done: hyperinflation, peribronchial thickening, atelectasis.
Admit based on **work of breathing and oxygen sats**. Supportive: oxygen, hydration, **nasal suction**.
**No routine bronchodilators or steroids** (AAP). Trial salbutamol only with strong family asthma history. No ribavirin.
Prevent: **palivizumab 15 mg/kg** for preterm and heart disease. RSV spreads by contact: **hand washing**.

sections.title: Asthma severity classes
notes: **Intermittent**: symptoms 2 days a week or less, nights 2 a month or less, normal lung function. **Salbutamol as needed only**.
**Mild persistent**: over 2 days a week, over 2 nights a month, FEV1 over 80%. **Daily low-dose inhaled steroid**.
**Moderate persistent**: daily symptoms, **nights over once a week**, FEV1 60 to 80%. Medium-dose inhaled steroid (or low dose plus LABA).
**Severe persistent**: all day, most nights, FEV1 under 60%. Medium to high dose steroid plus LABA, consider oral steroid burst.
Case: daily symptoms, worse with football, waking 3 to 4 nights a week: **moderate persistent**.

sections.title: Asthma triggers and presentation
notes: Risks: parental asthma, **eczema**, aeroallergen sensitization, food allergy, **eosinophils over 4%**.
**Most common trigger: viral infection (rhinovirus)**. Also allergens, smoke, exercise, NSAIDs, beta blockers.
Wheeze, but **no wheeze doesn't rule it out**: cough-only asthma, night or exercise cough, **chest tightness or pain**.

sections.title: Severe asthma signs
notes: Talking in words, agitated, tachypnea, retractions, **silent chest is worse, not better**.
**Pulsus paradoxus over 20 mmHg**, sats under 91%.
Impending failure: **normal or rising CO2**, bradycardia, drowsiness, confusion, paradoxical breathing.

sections.title: Status asthmaticus and exacerbations
notes: Oxygen, IV fluids, **continuous salbutamol plus ipratropium**, **early IV steroids** (work in 4 to 6 hours). **Magnesium sulfate** if not improving.
Exacerbation at home: salbutamol for at least 5 days, **oral steroids 3 to 10 days**, early follow-up. **No antibiotics** (atelectasis is not pneumonia).

sections.title: Asthma diagnosis and exercise-induced asthma
notes: Clinical diagnosis. Spirometry shows obstruction and response. **Exercise challenge** with spirometry before and after.
Chest x-ray not needed (hyperinflation, atelectasis). Foreign body can mimic asthma. Skin or blood allergy testing.
Exercise-induced: **warm up**, **salbutamol 15 minutes before exercise**. Needing more: add inhaled steroid or montelukast.

sections.title: Asthma medicines
notes: Needing lots of salbutamol means **poor control**. Salbutamol works in 15 minutes, lasts 3 to 4 hours.
**LABA (salmeterol, formoterol) never alone**: risk of asthma death. Beta agonist side effects: tremor, tachycardia, **hypokalemia**.
**Inhaled steroids are the main controller**. Slight first-year growth slowing, final height unchanged, **poorly controlled asthma slows growth more**. Rinse mouth (thrush), spacer.
Montelukast: add-on, helps allergic rhinitis, viral wheeze, exercise asthma.

sections.title: Asthma risk and inhaler devices
notes: Future asthma risk under 3: **3 or more wheezing episodes a year**, eczema, parental asthma, allergic rhinitis, wheeze without colds, eosinophils over 4%.
**MDI with spacer** is as good as a nebulizer and faster (**4 puffs = 2.5 mg nebulized**). Mask with spacer for young kids. Dry powder inhaler from about age 4.

sections.title: Pneumonia: causes by clue
notes: Case: 5-year-old, fever, cough, grunting, right crackles, **right middle lobe consolidation**.
Infant afebrile staccato cough with interstitial infiltrates: **Chlamydia trachomatis**. **School age: Mycoplasma** (walking pneumonia). Pertussis: paroxysms, no fever.

Histoplasmosis (Ohio and Mississippi valleys), coccidioidomycosis (California, Arizona), Legionella (water), tularemia (rabbits, ticks), psittacosis (parakeets), Q fever (farm animals). Varicella and measles cause pneumonia.

sections.title: Pneumonia: signs
notes: No fever or no cough doesn't rule it out. Can present as **chest or abdominal pain**. **Grunting** can signal impending failure.
**Tachypnea is the most sensitive and specific sign**: over 50 at 2 to 12 months, over 40 at 1 to 5 years, over 20 after 5.
Bacterial pneumonia unlikely with **no fever, no tachypnea, normal work of breathing and normal exam**.

sections.title: Pneumonia: diagnosis and treatment
notes: Clinical diagnosis. Outpatients usually need **no chest x-ray**. X-ray if complicated, prolonged fever, worsening, or febrile infant with no source. **X-ray lags clinical recovery**.
Outpatient: **high-dose amoxicillin 80 to 90 mg/kg/day**. Over 5 years (Mycoplasma): **azithromycin**.
Admit: sepsis, toxic, hypoxia, can't drink, failed outpatient treatment. Inpatient: ampicillin or **ceftriaxone**. Staph: vancomycin or clindamycin.
Should improve in **48 to 96 hours**. If not: x-ray for empyema, TB, foreign body, CF, sequestration, aspiration.

sections.title: Pleural effusion and empyema
notes: Case: 15-month-old worsening on day 3 of pneumonia, decreased right breath sounds, **blunted costophrenic angle, shift to the left**: parapneumonic effusion or empyema.
**Exudate** (Light): fluid to serum protein over 0.5, LDH ratio over 0.6, or LDH over 2/3 of upper normal. **Chylothorax is the most common newborn effusion**.
Dullness, absent breath sounds, rub. **Ultrasound shows loculation**, CT for complicated cases. Thoracentesis, antibiotics, oxygen.

sections.title: Tension pneumothorax and pneumothorax
notes: Sudden collapse, absent breath sounds, **tracheal shift away**, sats 60%: **tension pneumothorax**. **Decompress immediately, no x-ray first**.
Primary spontaneous: **tall thin males**, apical blebs, smoking. Secondary: lung disease, trauma, loud music.
Under 5%: oxygen and observe. Over 5%, recurrent or tension: **chest tube**.

sections.title: Aspiration and hydrocarbons
notes: Gastric aspirate over 0.8 mL/kg or pH under 2.5: chemical pneumonitis. X-ray changes can take **1 to 2 days**.
**Hydrocarbons** (gasoline, kerosene, lamp oil): can look well then crash. **Never empty the stomach or induce vomiting**.
Suction the airway, don't neutralize. **No prophylactic antibiotics or steroids**, even with fever.
**Asymptomatic with normal x-ray: observe 4 to 6 hours**. Abnormal x-ray: admit.

sections.title: Foreign body aspiration
notes: **Under 3 years**, nuts (peanuts a third), hot dogs, grapes.
Choking episode, then a **symptom-free interval**, then chronic cough or **wheeze not responding to asthma treatment**. Exam can be normal.
**A witnessed choking episode is never ignored**. Right main bronchus most often.
Chest x-ray **normal in 10 to 30%** (radiolucent). Look for **unilateral air trapping** (inspiratory and expiratory or decubitus films). **Rigid bronchoscopy** if suspected, even with a normal x-ray.

sections.title: Lung abscess
notes: Cavity over 2 cm from aspiration or infection. Risk: dysphagia, developmental delay, poor airway protection, neuromuscular weakness.
Fever, cough, sputum, hemoptysis, weight loss. **Air-fluid level** on x-ray.
**Clindamycin** (anaerobes): IV 2 to 3 weeks, then oral to 4 to 6 weeks.

sections.title: Pulmonary sequestration
notes: Non-functioning lung with **systemic arterial supply**, no airway connection.

**Extralobar**: more common, own pleura, presents in infancy, with **congenital diaphragmatic hernia**. **Intralobar**: inside normal pleura, **recurrent pneumonia** in older kids. Both usually left lower.
CT with contrast. **Surgical removal**.

sections.title: Bronchogenic cyst, lobar emphysema, CPAM
notes: **Bronchogenic cyst**: **sharply demarcated spherical mass in the middle mediastinum near the carina**. Dysphagia, cough, recurrent pneumonia. Remove surgically.
Congenital lobar emphysema: air in, not out, **one lobe overinflates**, newborn distress.
**CPAM (cystic adenomatoid malformation)**: air-filled cysts, newborn distress or later recurrent infections. Surgical removal.

sections.title: Primary ciliary dyskinesia and bronchiectasis
notes: **PCD**: autosomal recessive, impaired mucociliary clearance, **situs inversus** (Kartagener) in some, **male infertility**. Chronic wet cough, sinusitis, **otitis media**, bronchiectasis. Electron microscopy of cilia.
**Bronchiectasis**: most common cause **cystic fibrosis**. Chronic productive cough, crackles, clubbing. **CT is best**.

sections.title: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia
notes: Chronic lung disease of extreme preemies from ventilation, oxygen, barotrauma.
Tachypnea, increased work, **frequent desaturations**. X-ray: low volumes, atelectasis, hyperinflation, interstitial emphysema.
Surfactant, gentle ventilation, **permissive hypercapnia**, avoid too much oxygen (ROP), diuretics, treat PDA, watch for pulmonary hypertension and reflux.

sections.title: Pulmonary hemosiderosis
notes: Repeated alveolar bleeding with hemosiderin-laden macrophages: **lung symptoms plus severe iron deficiency anemia**.
Idiopathic most common. Also heart failure, Goodpasture, granulomatosis with polyangiitis, HSP, **cow's milk (Heiner syndrome)**.
Hemoptysis, wheeze, microcytic anemia, bilateral infiltrates. **Steroids** for idiopathic.

sections.title: Sarcoidosis
notes: Non-caseating granulomas, more common in Black patients. **Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy**, can be incidental.
Fever, cough, erythema nodosum. **Hypercalcemia, hypercalciuria, high ACE level**. Steroids for symptomatic cases.

sections.title: Cystic fibrosis: lungs and newborn
notes: Autosomal recessive **CFTR, chromosome 7, F508del** most common.
Chronic cough (**test if over 6 weeks**), barrel chest, crackles, clubbing, **nasal polyps (red flag)**. Pathogens: **S aureus early, Pseudomonas later**.
**Meconium ileus** in 15 to 20%: distension, vomiting, no meconium, ground-glass bubbly bowel. **Gastrografin enema** diagnostic and therapeutic.

sections.title: Cystic fibrosis: GI and other
notes: Pancreatic insufficiency: failure to thrive, **bulky greasy foul stools**, **A, D, E, K deficiency** (night blindness, low bone density, neuropathy and hemolysis, bleeding).
Delayed puberty, **azoospermia**, **distal intestinal obstruction syndrome** in teens (missed enzymes), **rectal prolapse**, biliary cirrhosis, **CF-related diabetes**.

sections.title: Cystic fibrosis: diagnosis and treatment
notes: Newborn screen first. **Sweat chloride is the gold standard**: **over 60** diagnostic (**over 40 under 6 months**). Repeat to confirm.
False positives: eczema, adrenal insufficiency, ectodermal dysplasia, nephrogenic DI, G6PD, hypothyroidism, malnutrition.
Pancreatic tests: fecal elastase, **72-hour fecal fat**. Treatment: enzymes, vitamins, bronchodilators, hypertonic saline, **dornase**, antibiotics. Survival now past 50.

sections.title: Obstructive sleep apnea
notes: Primary snoring: no apneas or gas exchange problems. OSA: **apneas, poor sleep, CO2 retention**, can lead to **pulmonary hypertension and right heart failure**.
Risks: **big tonsils and adenoids**, obesity, midface hypoplasia, **Down syndrome**, neuromuscular disease, cerebral palsy.
Snoring with witnessed pauses, mouth breathing, morning headache, sleepiness. Can look like **ADHD** and cause **enuresis**.
**Polysomnography** is diagnostic. **Adenotonsillectomy first line**, CPAP otherwise. Post-op risk: pulmonary edema.

sections.title: Apnea and BRUE
notes: Central apnea: idiopathic most common, prematurity, infection, reflux, seizures, arrhythmia, **abuse**.
Awake events: **reflux most common**, then seizures. **RSV can present with apnea before bronchiolitis**.

sections.title: SIDS prevention
notes: **Back to sleep** under 1 year, tummy time only while awake and watched, **no smoking**.
Risks: prematurity, low birth weight, **co-sleeping**, prone sleep, overheating, young mother, poor prenatal care.
**Pacifier at sleep lowers SIDS risk** (once breastfeeding is established). **Apnea monitors don't reduce SIDS**.

sections.title: Pectus excavatum and carinatum
notes: Excavatum: with **Marfan, Ehlers-Danlos**. Usually asymptomatic, surgery only if physiologic compromise.
Carinatum: sternum pushed out, mostly cosmetic, reassure.
